subject: Throughput floor & per-tenant isolation request — Orthus Health
messages:
From: Alex Russo <alex.russo@orthus.health>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@orthus.health>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Throughput floor + per-tenant isolation request — Orthus Health

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare for a phased rollout of our patient-facing assistants, security and predictability of inference performance are top of mind. We validated projected peak traffic and have two requests we need Redwood to contractually commit to before we proceed to signature:

1) Throughput floor: a guaranteed baseline throughput for our Dedicated pool during business-critical windows (weekdays 08:00–20:00 PST) so we don't see degraded tail latency during coordinated traffic spikes. We put a tentative floor of 3k tokens/sec for sustained 30-minute windows in the request doc.

2) Per-tenant isolation: during high load we need per-customer isolation so that other tenants' spikes will not impact Orthus's tail latency. We understand this may require soft reservations or sub-pools — we're open to trade-offs.

I've attached a short request packet (orthus_sla_request.pdf) and a traffic export for April–May (traffic_profile_apr-may.csv). Our procurement lead is ready to move quickly once we have clear feasibility and a proposed commercial amendment.

Can you confirm who on your side should evaluate the technical feasibility and what a reasonable timeline looks like?

Appreciate it —
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
Orthus Health

Attachments: orthus_sla_request.pdf (application/pdf), traffic_profile_apr-may.csv (text/csv)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Russo <alex.russo@orthus.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput floor + per-tenant isolation request — Orthus Health

Alex — thanks for the packet and the sample traffic. Looping in Karthik (SRE/runtime) for a feasibility assessment and Marissa (AE) for commercial fit.

High level next steps I propose:
- Karthik: give a short assessment of options (soft reservations, sub-pools, isolation trade-offs) and any perf numbers we can reasonably commit to.
- Marissa: sketch a contractual amendment / pricing uplift and lead time for implementation.
- Lauren: consolidate and propose a pilot timeline (we typically do a 30-day warm-up/trial for new isolation configs).

Karthik/Marissa — can you look at the attachments and reply with feasibility + a recommended SLA amendment draft by EOD Monday (PST)? We need this in order to keep Orthus on the current procurement window.

Thanks —
Lauren
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alex Russo <alex.russo@orthus.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput floor + per-tenant isolation request — Orthus Health

Lauren / Alex — reviewed the traffic CSV and the request doc. Short summary and practical options: 

Summary observations:
- Peak windows look like short (10–40 min) coordinated bursts to the same endpoints, with spikes up to ~3.6k tokens/sec across the service.
- Steady-state traffic outside business windows is a small fraction of peak.

Feasible approaches (trade-offs):
A) Soft reservation + priority scheduling (recommended minimal disruption):
   - Keep a single dedicated pool but implement a per-tenant soft reservation that guarantees ~3k tokens/sec during configured business hours by using request prioritization and token-weighted fair queuing.
   - Expected impact: ~10–18% higher effective cost due to headroom and reduced batch-filling efficiency; latency during worst-case will still see some variance but we can cap 95th-percentile tail with targeted throttles and overflow routing.
   - Implementation time: 3–4 weeks to ship a guarded config on Dedicated, plus 1 week of controlled pilot.

B) Sub-pool isolation (stronger guarantee):
   - Provision a sub-pool (segregated set of reserved GPUs) for Orthus. This gives hard isolation and the best tail-latency predictability.
   - Expected impact: ~15–30% increase in committed capacity and cost (depends on sizing). Lead time: 6–8 weeks to reserve capacity and validate runtime scheduling.

C) Hybrid: soft reservations for now + scheduled sub-pool for critical windows.

What we can consider contractually: a temporary SLA addendum that guarantees a throughput floor (e.g., 3k tokens/sec sustained for 30 minutes during business hours) backed by remediation credits if we miss the target for reasons within Redwood control. For hard guarantees we should tie the stronger SLA to a sub-pool purchase so we can provision capacity exclusively.

Caveats: pre-warming KV caches and model warm-up is critical; without warm caches effective throughput drops and tail latency increases. We recommend an automated pre-warm job during your business-window start (we can run as part of onboarding).

I'll draft a short technical addendum with numbers and options — will send later today.

— Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Alex Russo <alex.russo@orthus.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 20:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput floor + per-tenant isolation request — Orthus Health

Alex — appreciate the patience. Based on Karthik's options, commercial notes below: 

Option A (soft reservation):
- Amendment: update Dedicated terms with a "throughput floor" clause limited to business hours and subject to pre-warm requirements.
- Pricing: +12% uplift on committed monthly spend to cover headroom.
- Commitment: 12-month term.
- Remediation: service credit up to 5% of monthly bill for qualifying SLA misses.
- Lead time: 3–5 weeks to configure and pilot.

Option B (sub-pool):
- Amendment: reserved sub-pool SKU added to contract (exact GPU count to be sized).
- Pricing: depends on size; rough estimate +25–35% on top of existing commitment.
- Commitment: 12-month minimum.
- Remediation: stronger SLA (higher credit cap) when sub-pool purchased.
- Lead time: 6–8 weeks (may require a capacity reservation).

Docs & next steps:
- I'll prepare a short amendment and a pricing worksheet; I'm happy to run an internal discount review if Orthus needs help landing within procurement thresholds.
- Marissa note: we should include a clause about maintenance windows and scheduled capacity changes.

Alex — do you want me to prepare a DocuSign amendment draft for Option A first (faster) while we size Option B? If you prefer Option B we should start PO and capacity reservation conversations ASAP.

Cheers —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Russo <alex.russo@orthus.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Throughput floor & per-tenant isolation request — Orthus Health

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround, team. To keep momentum and unblock procurement this week, here's a recommended path: 

1) Short-term: proceed with Option A (soft reservation + automated pre-warm). Marissa will issue a concise amendment and pricing worksheet. We propose a 30-day pilot after sign to validate sizing and tune priority policies.

2) Parallel: Karthik and team will begin sizing a potential sub-pool for Option B. If the pilot shows material benefits and Orthus wants a hard guarantee, we will transition to a sub-pool + stronger SLA.

3) Action items:
   - Alex: confirm you approve starting with Option A and whether procurement will accept a 12-month term with the uplift outlined.
   - Marissa: please send the DocuSign link for the Option A amendment + pricing worksheet.
   - Karthik: send the technical addendum (warm-up steps, expected token/sec numbers, monitoring hooks) so Orthus can include it in their security/compliance packet.

If we get sign-off today, Marissa will issue DocuSign and we can stand up the pilot config within 10 business days.

Onward —
Lauren
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
